newsitem.title: USA: Consumer group chides banks on campaign funding.
newsitem.headline: Consumer group chides banks on campaign funding.

text.p: Banks ranking in the top 100 student loan lenders contributed $2.3 million to congressional candidates through June 1996, with 72 percent going to Republicans, Citizen Action reported Thursday.

Citizen Action charged that the contributions were to support a Republican plan to end the government's new direct student loan program in favor of a larger subsidized program of private bank loans to college students.

Sen. Paul Simon, D-Ill., said the new direct loan program enacted in 1993 saved 10 million students an average of $190. The end of this program would shift $75.3 billion in student loans to private lenders, Citizen Action said.
